nodes.label: Spec 0004 rationale: One real primary path rationale (context, four options, 46 decisions taken with notes on the heavy ones, the locked packages, the evidence gathered for the spec, and the cross check findings)

Context of spec 0004: scopes 001 to 003 built the ground and no byte has gone from a client to PostgreSQL through POOL; scope 004 has to be right about a wire protocol, two TLS legs, two separate authentications, an identity map, durable authority, live evidence, limits and teardown at once; the safety contracts of spec 0001 are fixed, the review of scope 003 found three ways the authority functions could still open writes, the dependency tree is kept small, the source guard has to change the day a socket appears, and the team is two engineers with one workstation (R-24)

Spec 0004 option 1 (chosen): the whole thin path, wire code in two new crates, a topology snapshot between control and data, no client driver; one implementation of startup, TLS upgrade and SCRAM used by the data path and the probe; the cost is more first party protocol code and a large slice of fourteen build steps

Spec 0004 option 2 (rejected): a client driver, tokio-postgres, for the probe and other control SQL in pool-control; about 25 more packages, a second SCRAM implementation and a second TLS path for one query, and pool-control would then name the runtime and sockets

Spec 0004 option 3 (rejected): modules in the binary first, crates later; the fuzz target has to live in the fuzz/ directory of the crate it tests, the source guard could no longer say that framing code is pure, and spec 0001 already decided the four crates

Spec 0004 option 4 (rejected): two slices, authority on disk first and the session later; scope 004 would end without a client ever connecting, so none of PRD-001 AC-1, AC-3 or AC-4 would have evidence and the walking slice milestone would not be met; the same order is available inside one scope

Why spec 0004 takes option 1: it is the only option that meets the scope text, the safety contracts and the guards at the same time; the pieces are small when the path is narrow (two client messages and nine backend messages, SCRAM without channel binding, one probe query); the size of the slice is the real cost and the build plan answers it: authority on disk first (step 8), the session second (step 10), breadth last (step 11), and if the estimate runs over the cut is after step 10

Decisions taken in spec 0004: the architect session ran in the auto decision mode, so each of the 46 choices is the recommended option taken without asking, with the runner up and the way back; heavy marks a public contract, a format, a part of the security model or a change to an accepted spec; decisions 1 to 16 and decision 46, added after acceptance, are heavy

0004 decision 1 (heavy): the number of findings from one file is limited (0003 Follow-up 11, written there as the user's decision): the first 20000 are kept, the rest are counted and the report says how many were left out, plus the output buffer; runner up: the buffer only

0004 decision 2 (heavy): control characters above U+007F and direction characters are not allowed in a name or a path (0003 Follow-up 12): a closed list is refused with config.invalid_value; runner up: keep the list of spec 0003 and escape names in every later output
0004 decision 3 (heavy): the frontend authenticates with SCRAM-SHA-256 against a verifier file per principal; runner up: a client certificate first
0004 decision 4 (heavy): channel binding is neither offered nor used, on neither leg, in this slice; runner up: build SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS now
0004 decision 5 (heavy): a verifier lives in a [[principal]] table with verifier_file; runner up: a verifier_file key in every identity entry
0004 decision 6 (heavy): the session accepts Query and Terminate after login and everything else ends it with 0A000; runner up: pass every message through unchanged
0004 decision 7 (heavy): pool run refuses to start when the journal state is not ready; runner up: start and refuse every login with 57P03
0004 decision 8 (heavy): bootstrap and reading the authority ID are two commands of pool, bootstrap and show-authority; runner up: create apps/pool-cli now
0004 decision 9 (heavy): POOL generates the SQLSTATEs of the spec table: FATAL only, constant text, one code per situation; runner up: reuse the texts of PostgreSQL, or XX000 for everything POOL adds
0004 decision 10 (heavy): a running session is ended when admission closes later on a positive conflict and not on silence; runner up: never, until scope 008 decides

0004 decision 11 (heavy): the probe gets the timeline from plain SQL, the WAL file name on a primary and the greatest known value on a node in recovery; runner up: a replication connection with IDENTIFY_SYSTEM

0004 decision 12 (heavy): a Ready state learns of a latch set after the start (point m1) through two functions in pool-control, one that sets the latch in memory and one that takes the revision from a receipt of the journal; runner up: read and classify the journal again after every write

0004 decision 13 (heavy): only pool-control may build a journal value (point m2): other crates get an opaque JournalRead and a source guard refuses four names outside the crate; runner up: private fields and one checked constructor

0004 decision 14 (heavy): the sample rule does not get stricter (point m3); the caller is fenced instead: a board with one sample per node, a clamp of now inside build_snapshot and a guard that lets only pool-control call writer_admission; runner up: a new reason evidence.sample_unusable
0004 decision 15 (heavy): rule W3 works with one file of bare, deny and allow lines once sockets exist; runner up: one baseline file per crate
0004 decision 16 (heavy): the crypto library is aws-lc-rs, which rustls uses by default and the security requirements name; runner up: ring
0004 decision 17 (not heavy): pool-protocol and pool-core are both created now; runner up: modules in the binary first
0004 decision 18 (not heavy): the probe talks to PostgreSQL through the backend connection of pool-core; runner up: tokio-postgres
0004 decision 19 (not heavy): SQLite is linked through rusqlite with bundled; runner up: the SQLite of the host

0004 decision 20 (not heavy): for a user name that is no principal POOL runs the full exchange with a made up verifier; runner up: refuse at once with 28P01, which would let a client list the principals
0004 decision 21 (not heavy): a startup parameter POOL does not forward is refused with 0A000; runner up: ignore it
0004 decision 22 (not heavy): POOL sends nothing as BackendKeyData; runner up: a random key that matches nothing
0004 decision 23 (not heavy): a request for protocol 3.2 is answered with NegotiateProtocolVersion for 3.0; runner up: refuse
0004 decision 24 (not heavy): sessions get the writer by reading the route view built from the snapshot (point m6); runner up: call writer_admission per login with an index of the samples

0004 decision 25 (not heavy): the expiry has the range 1000 to 60000 ms, at least period plus timeout, read from the configuration by build_snapshot (point n2); runner up: a checked expiry type in pool-control
0004 decision 26 (not heavy): the probe keeps its connection, one per node, opened again after a failure; runner up: a new connection for every sample
0004 decision 27 (not heavy): one writer runs without a thread through &mut self, the blocking pool of the runtime and the directory lock; runner up: a thread of its own with a channel
0004 decision 28 (not heavy): the state directory is locked with File::try_lock on pool.lock; runner up: the exclusive locking mode of SQLite
0004 decision 29 (not heavy): the service account is the owner of the state directory; runner up: the effective user, read through a new dependency
0004 decision 30 (not heavy): a client whose backend is lost gets 08007 with a query in flight, 08006 without and nothing in the middle of a message; runner up: always close without a message
0004 decision 31 (not heavy): the session permits are taken after authentication and a separate cap bounds handshakes; runner up: one connection limit at accept
0004 decision 32 (not heavy): the relay buffer is not a key but a constant of 65536 bytes; runner up: a key in [limits]
0004 decision 33 (not heavy): POOL accepts SCRAM-SHA-256 only from a node; runner up: also a clear text password over TLS, or no proof at all
0004 decision 34 (not heavy): a backend password may hold printable ASCII only; runner up: any text, with SASLprep
0004 decision 35 (not heavy): the new licenses enter deny.toml as five exceptions by crate; runner up: two more lines in the general list
0004 decision 36 (not heavy): the log lines are written by a first party tracing::Subscriber; runner up: tracing-subscriber with a custom format
0004 decision 37 (not heavy): refusals are logged counted, one line per reason and second; runner up: one event per refusal
0004 decision 38 (not heavy): psql runs in the PostgreSQL container in the integration check, reaching POOL on the host; runner up: on the host
0004 decision 39 (not heavy): case 17 is repaired by the script making a feature of its own in its copy; runner up: point the case at the scope 005 file
0004 decision 40 (not heavy): the dependencies are added in one step, before the code that uses them; runner up: each step adds its own
0004 decision 41 (not heavy): a command says that a valid file is not enough through two views and the code config.incomplete; runner up: make the keys required in the schema
0004 decision 42 (not heavy): the runtime flavor is multi thread, with four blocking threads at most; runner up: current thread
0004 decision 43 (not heavy): the salted password is not derived at every backend login: the two keys are kept per credential, salt and count; runner up: derive every time
0004 decision 44 (not heavy): a log line does not wait for stderr: a bounded queue and one writing task, and a full queue drops and counts; runner up: write in place
0004 decision 45 (not heavy): a client whose session POOL ends gets 08007 with a query in flight and 57P01 without; runner up: always 57P01

0004 decision 46 (heavy): added on 2026-11-15, after acceptance, from a finding of the developer of step 5: invalid-unknown-key.toml of spec 0001 uses [listener] as its unknown table and this slice makes that table known; the fixture and two in memory tests name the table no_table, and finding, line, column and output stay the same bytes; runner up: keep the fixture text and let its result change to three config.missing_key findings, with an exception in 0004 AC-5

Note on 0004 decision 1, the limit on findings: spec 0003 measured two million findings and 500 MiB from one 1 MiB file and said a buffer alone does not bound it; this slice is the first in which the daemon validates at a start; a fixed count bounds every shape of input; the number has to be above 17268, which 0003 AC-15 promises for made input 3, and 20000 is the next round number; the file is rejected as a whole either way, so SEC-12 is untouched

Note on 0004 decision 2, names: bytes in a startup packet cannot inject anything; the risk is in every later output, an escape sequence in a terminal or two entries that look the same on a screen; refusing the characters once, in the one place that reads the file, cannot be forgotten; no deployment exists, so today the cost is zero

Note on 0004 decisions 3 to 5, the frontend proof: the decision ledger already says terminated SCRAM over TLS; a verifier is what PostgreSQL itself stores, so POOL never sees the password; it belongs to the principal and not to the pair of principal and database; channel binding needs the hash of the server certificate under the algorithm of its own signature, which needs a certificate parser, so it waits for scope 006 and POOL does not advertise what it cannot do (SEC-3)

Note on 0004 decision 6, the subset: passing everything through would forward messages whose state POOL does not model (an error in the middle of a pipeline, an abandoned COPY, a function call); the protocol engine page says unsupported paths fail explicitly; a narrow path that is fully understood is the point of a walking slice

Note on 0004 decision 7, refusing to start: both answers are closed and the difference is who notices; a daemon that runs and refuses everything looks healthy to a service manager and has no status read until scope 008, and a daemon that exits with a named finding is seen at once

Note on 0004 decision 9, SQLSTATEs: client libraries act on the class of a code (08 the connection, 53 resources, 57 the operator); using the codes PostgreSQL uses for the nearest situation lets them do the right thing without knowing POOL; 08007 is the standard code for a transaction whose outcome is unknown, exactly the lost COMMIT; constant text keeps names out of error messages

Note on 0004 decision 10, ending sessions: spec 0001 says a primary profile stays on its lease and the overview says existing traffic may continue when freshness is lost; neither says it may continue when a probe has positively shown the node is no longer the writer, and the invariant 'keep writes on the verified primary' says it may not; silence and contradiction are already different things in the rules of spec 0003

Note on 0004 decision 11, the timeline: on a primary the WAL file name of the write position gives the current timeline and any role may ask for it; on a node in recovery plain SQL does not show the replay timeline, and the replication protocol needs the REPLICATION attribute, which is against SEC-5 for a monitor; taking the greatest value the node shows can only close earlier and never opens anything; scope 007 qualifies it on a real replica

Note on 0004 decisions 12 to 14, the three findings of the review of scope 003: they are written up in the update of spec 0003 because they change its interface; the common thread is that a rule should not rest on a caller remembering something; the stricter sample rule was the first draft and was dropped when the tests of 0003 AC-11 turned out to assert an open answer for exactly those two inputs

Note on 0004 decision 15, the guard: the rule protects that no crate grows a socket by accident and that control never gets the means to do the work of core; a list of exceptions by path on top of a list that covers everything keeps both, and a new crate is covered before anyone thinks about it

Note on 0004 decision 16, the crypto library: aws-lc-rs and ring were both resolved and built in the pinned Linux image on 2026-11-15 and need the same two licenses; ring is smaller; aws-lc-rs is what the security requirements name and rustls selects by default, and it brings no duplicate package, while ring would need the first skip entry in deny.toml; either can be swapped for the other later

Note on 0004 decision 46, the fixture: it is marked heavy because it changes the text of a fixture that an accepted spec quotes, and it changes nothing a user can see; listener was only ever a stand in for 'a table this build does not know', and keeping the name would have changed the meaning, the result and the evidence of 0001 AC-7; a name of the same length was chosen so that no position can move, checked by running the binary; the developer had proposed frontend, which is a glossary term that a later slice could make a table

Locked packages of spec 0004: 70 third party packages resolved on 2026-11-15 with Cargo 1.100.0 in a scratch project outside the repository, each with version, declared license, whether it is new in this slice and whether it is built for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu; among them aws-lc-rs 1.19.0, aws-lc-sys 0.47.0, libsqlite3-sys 0.40.0, rusqlite 0.42.0, rustls 0.23.46, rustls-webpki 0.103.17, subtle 2.6.1, tokio 1.54.1, tokio-rustls 0.26.6, tracing 0.1.44 and untrusted 0.9.0; the real workspace adds its five members

Spec 0004 locked packages that are not built: ring, getrandom 0.2.17, windows-sys 0.52.0 and the windows-targets family are in the lockfile because rustls-webpki can use ring; cargo deny does not count them as duplicates because the feature that would use them is off; rule W1 compares names as a sorted list, so getrandom and windows-sys are each listed twice in the baseline

Evidence gathered for spec 0004 on 2026-11-15 on the workstation (macOS, Docker Desktop 29.9.2, aarch64), none of it evidence for a criterion: the dependency set resolves to 70 packages; cargo deny fails on ISC and BSD-3-Clause only and passes with the five exceptions on the scratch lockfile and the pool-config fuzz lockfile; with ring it also fails on a duplicate windows-sys; the native code builds in rust:1.100.0-slim-bookworm in 12 seconds with gcc only and prints sqlite 3.54.1; the fixture image digest was inspected and not pulled; the probe query returned one row for a LOGIN only role on PostgreSQL 18.6; in_hot_standby off is among the parameter status messages

Not checked for spec 0004 and left to the build to find: whether psql 18 is content without BackendKeyData (the runner up of decision 22 is the way out), whether the Debian 12 image holds openssl, the gateway address on a Linux engine, and the fuzz build on the hosted runner

Cross check findings of spec 0004: the draft was read by a second model (Claude Opus, read only, with no part in writing it) on 2026-11-15, asked first for decision completeness; its verdict was 'accept after fixes'; under the auto decision mode the recommended fix was taken for each of the 16 findings and the 7 soundness findings S1 to S7, all applied in index.md and, where they touch it, in the update of spec 0003

0004 cross check finding 1: the wrong identity case of AC-14 would have failed at TLS or login and never reached the identity rule; the certificates are made once, both containers get the same certificate, roles and passwords, and the test waits for evidence.writer_identity in the log

0004 cross check finding 2: toward a node the SCRAM header was not said, and with y PostgreSQL refuses the login as a downgrade; the backend connection now states the header n, the empty name, the nonce, c=biws, the nonce check and the e= answer

0004 cross check finding 3: a guard on the name StoredAuthority does not stop code that holds a StoreProbe from changing it; other crates get an opaque JournalRead, the guard refuses StoredAuthority, StoreProbe, classify_startup and plan_bootstrap outside pool-control, and 0003 AC-19 was rewritten
0004 cross check finding 4: select! needs the feature macros of tokio; the features macros and io-std are adopted and the lockfile count is 70, with tokio-macros new

0004 cross check finding 5: no safe way to set the umask aside, and an empty journal file after a crash would block bootstrap for good; the binary creates the file with mode 0o600 and sets the mode again, an empty database counts as absent, and AC-11 says 'no journal file'

0004 cross check findings 6 to 8 on the fixture: the SQL file of AC-18 truncates its table first and uses fixed keys and values; every fixture name starts with pz7_ so the redaction test can search for it; the verifier is read from a role made with NOLOGIN and dropped at once, so the principal cannot log in to PostgreSQL

0004 cross check findings 9 to 12: when NegotiateProtocolVersion is sent and a CancelRequest after TLS are stated under Startup; the log writer is installed after the bind, so listener.failed is a finding; the runtime resolves a host name at each attempt; an accept error is counted and followed by a wait of 100 ms, and the descriptor budget is stated

0004 cross check findings 13 to 16: build plan tracing was fixed in the tests table, the coverage table and the guard format; the report line counts the kept findings; things that happen after the answer are polled every 50 ms for at most 2 seconds; the script tells Docker Desktop from a Linux engine by the text of docker info

0004 cross check soundness finding S1: PBKDF2 at every backend login shares four blocking threads with the probe, so a burst of logins could close the cluster; the derived keys are kept per credential, salt and count (decision 43)

0004 cross check soundness finding S2: a round that waits for the journal delays the closed snapshot while the old open one is still fresh; the round works in memory and is published first, and the write follows (decision 12, 0003 AC-17)

0004 cross check soundness findings S3 to S7: a latch cannot be cleared in this slice (stated under Consequences); 57P01 with a query in flight hid an unknown outcome, so it is 08007 (decision 45); log writes go through a bounded queue and one writing task (decision 44); the made up verifier uses the count of the first principal's verifier and not 4096; one address can hold every handshake permit (stated as not defended)

Facts the spec 0004 cross check corrected: set_buffer_limit of rustls bounds what is queued for sending and not received plain text; a read only open of a WAL database may create the two side files, so AC-10 speaks of the content of the main file; PGOPTIONS makes a client send options, which is refused; not taken over: the claim that Cargo prints no warning for an unused dependency of a member; not changed: guard lines for ApprovedTopology and Quarantine, because with StoreProbe, classify_startup and plan_bootstrap fenced neither type can reach a function that reads it from outside the crate

hyperedges.label: The three decisions of spec 0004 that close the review findings m1, m2 and m3 of scope 003 in code (decisions 12 to 14), with their common note
